methodological_rigor.justification: The study proposes SpectraNet, a deep learning model for colonoscopy polyp segmentation combining a frozen SAM2 backbone with two novel components: a Spectral-Guided Boundary Enhancement module (SGBE) leveraging frequency-domain processing, and a Frequency-guided Spectral Mixture of Experts (FS-MoE) with heterogeneous expert specialization. Evaluation on three benchmark datasets (PolypSegDataset, Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinicDB) is standard practice for this task. Performance metrics (mDice, mIoU, mRecall, mPrecision) are appropriate. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component. However, key limitations include: parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) freezes the SAM2 backbone, so only 2.75M parameters are trainable, limiting the comparison with fully fine-tuned baselines; no external validation dataset or clinical colonoscopy cohort is used; inter-observer variability in ground-truth annotations is not assessed; and the clinical deployment pathway or regulatory considerations for AI-assisted polyp detection are not discussed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a computer vision/AI methodology paper evaluated on public benchmark datasets (LoE 5), the clinical relevance depends on whether improved polyp segmentation accuracy translates to patient outcomes. The paper demonstrates incremental improvements over prior methods (mDice 90.46%/93.16%/93.27% on three datasets) but does not address clinical integration, prospective validation in endoscopy workflows, or patient-level outcomes. Polyp segmentation is clinically important for colorectal cancer prevention, but this work remains a technical benchmark study without clinical trial evidence.

reporting_quality.justification: The architecture, training configuration, and evaluation datasets are sufficiently described to allow replication. Ablation studies systematically evaluate the contribution of each novel module. Comparison with multiple prior methods on established public benchmarks is provided. However, no formal AI/ML reporting guideline (TRIPOD-AI, CLAIM) is cited; the annotation process and inter-rater agreement for ground truth masks are not described; statistical significance of performance differences between methods is not formally tested (only point estimates provided). Code availability is mentioned or the datasets are publicly available, enabling partial reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The combination of SAM2 with spectral-domain frequency analysis for polyp boundary enhancement is a novel technical contribution. The heterogeneous FS-MoE expert design (edge detection, texture analysis, regional semantics) addresses a genuine limitation of single-pathway architectures for polyp segmentation. However, SAM2 adaptation for medical image segmentation is an active area with multiple contemporaneous publications, and the performance gains over prior state-of-the-art are incremental rather than transformative. The approach represents a meaningful but not breakthrough advance in technical methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly structured with appropriate sections describing the architecture, training details, experimental setup, and ablation analysis. The technical description of SGBE and FS-MoE modules is reasonably detailed. Qualitative segmentation examples are provided. However, the clinical motivation is briefly addressed and the translation from benchmark performance to clinical utility is not convincingly argued. Some figures describing the architecture could benefit from additional annotation for clarity. Overall the writing is adequate for a technical AI/ML paper.

key_strengths: Novel combination of SAM2 frozen backbone with spectral-domain boundary enhancement (SGBE) and heterogeneous mixture-of-experts (FS-MoE) for polyp segmentation is technically innovative
Competitive performance across three public benchmark datasets (mDice 90.46%/93.16%/93.27%) with parameter-efficient design (2.75M trainable parameters)
Systematic ablation studies validate the contribution of each architectural component
Comparison with multiple prior state-of-the-art methods on established benchmarks
key_concerns: No external clinical validation; performance is limited to public benchmark datasets with no prospective endoscopy cohort evaluation
Statistical significance of performance differences from competing methods is not formally tested (p-values absent)
Inter-rater agreement for ground-truth segmentation masks is not discussed, limiting understanding of the annotation quality ceiling
No discussion of computational requirements, inference speed, or clinical deployment considerations relevant to real-time endoscopy use
chief_reviewer.rationale: A technically sound DL polyp segmentation paper proposing a novel spectral-guided architecture built on SAM2 with incremental but meaningful performance improvements over prior methods on standard benchmarks. The work is suitable for a mid-tier medical imaging or AI journal with minor revisions primarily to add statistical significance testing for performance comparisons and to better address the clinical translation gap.
